proofs.proof_tex:
The specialization \(C_T=1+\delta_T\), its normalized radius, and its adaptive depth are the objects recorded by \(\mathrm{def{:}local\text{-}frontier\text{-}handle}\).  Apply \(\mathrm{thm{:}uniform\text{-}overlap\text{-}frontier}\) with \(C=C_T\).  The definition \(\mathrm{def{:}overlap\text{-}distance\text{-}radius}\) gives exactly
\[
 q_{C_T}=\frac{C_T-1}{C_T}=\frac{\delta_T}{1+\delta_T}.
\]
The uniform theorem supplies the two risk inequalities with constants depending only on \(t_0,\zeta,M_1,M_2\), and \(\mathrm{def{:}history\text{-}depth}\) supplies the displayed observable estimator.  The ratio of the second risk term to the first is
\[
 \frac{T^{-\beta}q_T^{2(1-\beta)}}{T^{-1}}
 =(Tq_T^2)^{1-\beta}.
\]
Because \(0<\beta<1\), this ratio is bounded when \(Tq_T^2=O(1)\) and diverges when \(Tq_T^2\to\infty\).  Moreover \(\delta_T\to0\) implies \(q_T/\delta_T=(1+\delta_T)^{-1}\to1\), so \(q_T\asymp T^{-1/2}\) is equivalent to \(C_T-1=\delta_T\asymp T^{-1/2}\).  On the nonparametric side of the elbow, the definition of \(\kappa_T(C_T)\), together with the fact that its \(T/2\) cap is eventually inactive, gives \(\kappa_T(C_T)=\lfloor\log(Tq_T^2)/\{2\log(1/\alpha)+\log L\}\rfloor\), which is of the asserted logarithmic order.  All conclusions therefore follow from the uniform theorem without any additional condition.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every \(M\in\mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C)\) and every integer \(0\le k\le\lfloor T/2\rfloor\), put \(\overline\theta_k=(T-k)^{-1}\sum_{t=k+1}^{T}Z_t(k)\).  Then
\[
 \left|E_M[Z_t(k)]-\theta(K,e)\right|\le2M_1q_C\alpha^k
\]
and
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_M(\overline\theta_k)
 \le\frac1{T-k}\left\{M_2L^{k+1}
 +4M_2\sum_{r=1}^{k}L^r
 +\frac{4M_1\sqrt{M_2}\,\alpha^k}{1-\alpha}\right\}.
\]
where the sum is zero when \(k=0\).  Consequently the clipped estimator satisfies
\[
 E_M[(\widehat\theta_k-\theta(K,e))^2]
 \le4M_1^2q_C^2\alpha^{2k}+\operatorname{Var}_M(\overline\theta_k).
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Write \(m(s,a):=E_K[Y_t\mid S_t=s,A_t=a]\).  The conditional moment envelope \(\mathrm{ass{:}bounded\text{-}reward}\) gives \(|m(s,a)|\le M_1\) and \(E_K[Y_t^2\mid S_t=s,A_t=a]\le M_2\); hence \(|g_e(s)|\le M_1\).  Sequential randomization in \(\mathrm{ass{:}sequential\text{-}ignorability}\), followed by the kernel factorization in \(\mathrm{ass{:}pomdp\text{-}kernel}\), permits cancellation of each behavior action probability against the corresponding factor \(\rho_j\).  Since \(S_{t-k}\sim d_b\) by \(\mathrm{ass{:}stationary\text{-}start}\), this gives, equation by equation,
\[
 E_M[Z_t(k)]=d_bP_e^kg_e,
 \qquad
 \theta(K,e)=d_eP_e^kg_e,
\]
where the second equality uses stationarity \(d_eP_e^k=d_e\) and \(\mathrm{def{:}target\text{-}value}\).

If \(C=1\), \(d_e\le d_b\) and equality of total masses imply \(d_e=d_b\).  If \(C>1\), define
\[
 \nu:=\frac{Cd_b-d_e}{C-1}.
\]
The pointwise overlap assumption makes \(\nu\) nonnegative, and normalization of \(d_b,d_e\) gives \(\nu(\mathcal S)=1\).  Thus
\[
 d_b=C^{-1}d_e+q_C\nu,
 \qquad
 \|d_b-d_e\|_{\mathrm{TV}}=q_C\|\nu-d_e\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le q_C. \tag{1}
\]
Iterating \(\mathrm{ass{:}uniform\text{-}contraction}\) under \(P_e\), and using that a function bounded by \(M_1\) changes expectations by at most \(2M_1\) times total variation, yields
\[
 |d_bP_e^kg_e-d_eP_e^kg_e|
 \le2M_1\|d_bP_e^k-d_eP_e^k\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \le2M_1q_C\alpha^k. \tag{2}
\]

We next prove the variance bound without a support bound on \(Y_t\).  The policy-overlap assumption gives \(0\le\rho_j\le L\) and hence \(\rho_j^2\le L\rho_j\).  Applying this inequality to all \(k+1\) ratios and then cancelling the remaining ratios as above gives
\[
 E_M[Z_t(k)^2]\le M_2L^{k+1}. \tag{3}
\]
For \(1\le h\le k\), the two weight windows overlap in exactly \(k+1-h\) actions.  Replace the square of every shared ratio by \(L\rho\).  The remaining product of one ratio for each action in the union changes the behavior actions on that union to target actions and therefore defines a probability law.  Cauchy--Schwarz under that hybrid law, together with the pointwise conditional second-moment bound at the two reward times, gives
\[
 E_M[|Z_t(k)Z_{t+h}(k)|]\le M_2L^{k+1-h}. \tag{4}
\]
Also \(|E_MZ_t(k)|\le M_1\), by its representation as \(d_bP_e^kg_e\).  Because \(M_1^2<M_2\) and \(L^{k+1-h}\ge1\), (4) implies
\[
 |\operatorname{Cov}_M(Z_t(k),Z_{t+h}(k))|
 \le2M_2L^{k+1-h},\qquad1\le h\le k. \tag{5}
\]

For \(h\ge k+1\), condition on the full history through \((Y_t,S_{t+1})\).  The Markov property and likelihood-ratio cancellation on the future block give
\[
 E_M[Z_{t+h}(k)\mid S_{t+1}]
 =\psi_h(S_{t+1}),
 \qquad
 \psi_h:=P_b^{h-k-1}P_e^kg_e. \tag{6}
\]
Under behavior stationarity, \(E_M\psi_h(S_{t+1})=d_bP_e^kg_e=E_MZ_t(k)\).  For every Markov kernel whose Dobrushin coefficient is at most \(\alpha\), the oscillation inequality \(\operatorname{osc}(Pf)\le\alpha\operatorname{osc}(f)\) follows by applying the total-variation contraction to two point masses.  Applying it to all \(h-1\) kernels in (6) gives
\[
 \operatorname{osc}(\psi_h)\le2M_1\alpha^{h-1}. \tag{7}
\]
Moreover, cancellation of one copy of each ratio and Cauchy--Schwarz give
\[
 E_M|Z_t(k)|
 =E_{\mathrm{hyb}}|Y_t|
 \le\{E_{\mathrm{hyb}}Y_t^2\}^{1/2}\le\sqrt{M_2}. \tag{8}
\]
Combining (6)--(8), and using that the mean of \(\psi_h(S_{t+1})\) lies between its minimum and maximum, yields
\[
 |\operatorname{Cov}_M(Z_t(k),Z_{t+h}(k))|
 \le2M_1\sqrt{M_2}\,\alpha^{h-1},\qquad h\ge k+1. \tag{9}
\]
This is the required disjoint-window control; it uses \(M_1\sqrt{M_2}\), not the false implication \(E|Z_t(k)|\le M_1\).

Let \(N=T-k\).  Stationarity and the covariance decomposition, followed by (3), (5), and (9), give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{Var}_M(\overline\theta_k)
 &\le\frac1N\left\{M_2L^{k+1}
 +4M_2\sum_{h=1}^{k}L^{k+1-h}
 +4M_1\sqrt{M_2}\sum_{h=k+1}^{\infty}\alpha^{h-1}\right\}\\
 &=\frac1N\left\{M_2L^{k+1}
 +4M_2\sum_{r=1}^{k}L^r
 +\frac{4M_1\sqrt{M_2}\,\alpha^k}{1-\alpha}\right\}.
 \end{aligned} \tag{10}
\]
Finally, \(|\theta(K,e)|\le M_1\) by the conditional mean envelope.  Projection onto \([-M_1,M_1]\) cannot increase squared distance from \(\theta(K,e)\).  Combining (2), the identity \(E[(\overline\theta_k-\theta)^2]=\operatorname{Var}(\overline\theta_k)+(E\overline\theta_k-\theta)^2\), and (10) proves all three conclusions.
added_lemmas.justification: This gives the radius-sensitive observable upper bound under the published conditional first- and second-moment envelope.
added_lemmas.gap: The calculation retains the normalized latent-overlap radius and controls overlapping and disjoint windows without a bounded-support shortcut.
added_lemmas.consumer: It supplies the attaining half of the uniform overlap frontier.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every fixed \(t_0>0\), \(\zeta>0\), \(0<M_1<\sqrt{M_2}\), \(C\ge1\), \(Q\ge1\), and \(v\in\{-1,+1\}\), the scaled signed-depth construction is a binary-action member of \(\mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C)\) for every \(T\).  If action one is taken with probability \(r\), its stationary law is
\[
 d_r(j,u)=\frac{w_j}{2}(1+u\varepsilon_Cr^j).
\]
Furthermore,
\[
 \frac12q_C\le\varepsilon_C\le q_C,
 \qquad
 \max_{j,u}\frac{d_e(j,u)}{d_b(j,u)}\le1+\varepsilon_C\le C,
 \qquad
 \theta(K,e)=vc_0\varepsilon_Cw_Q.
\]
At \(C=1\), both \(q_C\) and \(\varepsilon_C\) are zero and the two sign-indexed observed laws coincide.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
The construction uses finite alphabets, a time-homogeneous reward-transition kernel, and behavior actions drawn from the revealed policy independently of the past and hidden sign, so \(\mathrm{ass{:}pomdp\text{-}kernel}\) and \(\mathrm{ass{:}sequential\text{-}ignorability}\) hold.  Since \(L>1\), \(b(1)=L^{-1}\) and \(b(0)=1-L^{-1}\) are probabilities.  The only positive target action probability is \(e(1)=1\), and \(e(1)/b(1)=L\), proving \(\mathrm{ass{:}policy\text{-}overlap}\).

Every policy-induced row contains the common reset measure with coefficient at least \(1-\alpha\): at nonterminal depths this is the reset branch, while the terminal row is the reset measure itself.  Hence for each \(p\in\{b,e\}\) there is a Markov kernel \(R_p\) such that
\[
 P_p=(1-\alpha)\mathbf 1\nu_0+\alpha R_p.
\]
The common term cancels between two input laws, and Markov kernels contract total variation, so
\[
 \|\nu P_p-\nu'P_p\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \le\alpha\|\nu R_p-\nu'R_p\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \le\alpha\|\nu-\nu'\|_{\mathrm{TV}}.
\]
This proves \(\mathrm{ass{:}uniform\text{-}contraction}\), uniformly in \(Q\).

The policy-independent depth chain has transitions \(j\mapsto j+1\) with probability \(\alpha\) for \(j<Q\) and otherwise resets to zero.  The numbers \(w_j=(1-\alpha)\alpha^j/(1-\alpha^{Q+1})\) sum to one and satisfy \(w_j=\alpha w_{j-1}\) for \(j\ge1\), while the total flow into zero is \(w_Q+(1-\alpha)\sum_{j=0}^{Q-1}w_j=w_0\).  Thus \((w_j)\) is stationary.  Conditional on depth \(j\), the reset sign has mean \(\varepsilon_C\), and its mean survives each of the \(j\) intervening actions exactly when action one is chosen.  Under a policy choosing action one with probability \(r\), the conditional sign mean is therefore \(\varepsilon_Cr^j\), proving
\[
 d_r(j,u)=w_j(1+u\varepsilon_Cr^j)/2. \tag{11}
\]
In particular the stipulated initialization is \(d_b\), so \(\mathrm{ass{:}stationary\text{-}start}\) holds.

Put \(x=C-1\ge0\).  If \(0\le x\le1\), then \(\varepsilon_C=x/2\) and \(q_C=x/(1+x)\), whence \(q_C/2\le\varepsilon_C\le q_C\).  If \(x\ge1\), then \(\varepsilon_C=1/2\) and \(q_C=x/(1+x)\in[1/2,1)\), giving the same two inequalities.  This also covers \(C=1\), when both sides vanish.  From (11), with \(p=L^{-1}\),
\[
 \frac{d_e(j,+1)}{d_b(j,+1)}
 =\frac{1+\varepsilon_C}{1+\varepsilon_CL^{-j}}le1+\varepsilon_C,
 \qquad
 \frac{d_e(j,-1)}{d_b(j,-1)}
 =\frac{1-\varepsilon_C}{1-\varepsilon_CL^{-j}}\le1.
\]
If \(C\le2\), \(1+\varepsilon_C=1+(C-1)/2\le C\); if \(C\ge2\), \(1+\varepsilon_C=3/2\le C\).  Thus the latent stationary-overlap assumption holds.

Because \(M_2>M_1^2\), \(\gamma_0=\min\{M_1,\sqrt{M_2}\}=M_1>0\).  The reward probabilities are well defined because
\[
 0<\frac{c_0}{\gamma_0}=\frac{1-\alpha}{4}<\frac14.
\]
Their conditional mean has absolute value at most \(c_0\le M_1\), and their conditional second moment is \(\gamma_0^2=M_1^2<M_2\), proving the conditional moment envelope.  Finally, under the target policy, (11) gives \(E_e[U_t\mid J_t=Q]=\varepsilon_C\).  Rewards have zero conditional mean off depth \(Q\) and mean \(vc_0U_t\) at depth \(Q\), so \(\mathrm{def{:}target\text{-}value}\) gives
\[
 \theta(K,e)=vc_0\varepsilon_Cw_Q. \tag{12}
\]
At \(C=1\), \(\varepsilon_C=0\), so every reset sign is fair.  The transformation \(U_t\mapsto-U_t\) at every time preserves the hidden transition law and converts the reward kernel with \(v=+1\) into that with \(v=-1\).  Hence the two observed laws are identical, while (12) gives target value zero under both.
added_lemmas.justification: The scaled binary construction is a hard subclass of the full moment class and calibrates its perturbation uniformly to the overlap radius.
added_lemmas.gap: Its policy-invariant depth occupancy prevents the terminal stationary ratio from growing with depth.
added_lemmas.consumer: It supplies class membership, target separation, and the uniform comparison between the testing amplitude and the overlap radius.

added_lemmas.statement:
For the scaled signed-depth alternatives there are finite constants \(K_0\) and \(B_0\), depending only on \(t_0\), such that, uniformly in \(C\ge1\), \(Q\ge1\), \(T\ge1\), \(v\in\{-1,+1\}\), and every positive-probability observed history,
\[
 E_v[Y_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}^{\mathrm{obs}}]
 =vc_0\varepsilon_Ca_t^{(Q)}q_t^v,
 \qquad q_t^v\le K_0\alpha^Q,
\]
and
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(\mathbb P_{Q,+1}^{\mathrm{obs},T}\,\|\,
 \mathbb P_{Q,-1}^{\mathrm{obs},T})
 \le B_0T\varepsilon_C^2\alpha^{2Q}L^{-Q}.
\]
The bounds include every stationary initial window \(t\le Q\) and reveal neither reset times nor hidden depths.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Put \(p:=L^{-1}\) and \(\bar c:=c_0/\gamma_0=(1-\alpha)/4\).  Then \(0<\bar c<1-\alpha\), because \((1-\alpha)/4<1-\alpha\).  All action words have positive behavior probability, and all reward emissions have probability at least \((1-\bar c)/2>0\), so every conditional probability below is well defined.

We first identify the conditional reward mean.  If \(t>Q\), the event \(J_t=Q\) forces an uninterrupted episode beginning at depth zero at time \(t-Q\).  The preceding \(Q\) rewards in that episode occur at depths \(0,\ldots,Q-1\), hence are fair scaled Rademacher variables and carry no information about its reset sign.  That sign has mean \(\varepsilon_C\), and its mean is retained precisely when all actions \(A_{t-Q},\ldots,A_{t-1}\) equal one.  If \(t\le Q\), the same event forces \(J_1=Q-t+1\) and \(t-1\) uninterrupted advances.  By the behavior-stationary law in \(\mathrm{lem{:}scaled\text{-}signed\text{-}depth\text{-}radius}\), the initial sign conditional on that depth has mean \(\varepsilon_Cp^{Q-t+1}\); the observed preceding rewards are again nonterminal and fair.  Since \(\ell_t=\min\{Q,t-1\}\), both cases give
\[
 E_v[U_t\mathbf1\{J_t=Q\}\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}^{\mathrm{obs}}]
 =\varepsilon_Ca_t^{(Q)}q_t^v.
\]
The reward kernel then yields
\[
 E_v[Y_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}^{\mathrm{obs}}]
 =vc_0\varepsilon_Ca_t^{(Q)}q_t^v. \tag{13}
\]

We next bound the posterior terminal probability.  Condition also on the realized action window, which is legitimate because the constant observed state and \(\mathrm{ass{:}sequential\text{-}ignorability}\) make behavior actions independent Bernoulli\((p)\) draws under both alternatives.  For \(t>Q\), on \(J_t=Q\) the reward word from \(t-Q\) through \(t-1\) is fair, and its joint numerator conditional on \(\mathcal F_{t-Q-1}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) is
\[
 \Pr_v(J_{t-Q}=0\mid\mathcal F_{t-Q-1}^{\mathrm{obs}})\alpha^Q2^{-Q}
 \le\alpha^Q2^{-Q}.
\]
For \(t\le Q\), stationarity and the identity \(w_{Q-t+1}\alpha^{t-1}=w_Q\) make the corresponding numerator \(w_Q2^{-(t-1)}\le\alpha^Q2^{-(t-1)}\).  By the chain rule and (13), the denominator in either case is
\[
 2^{-\ell_t}\prod_{r=t-\ell_t}^{t-1}
 \left\{1+\frac{Y_r}{\gamma_0}\frac{E_v[Y_r\mid\mathcal F_{r-1}^{\mathrm{obs}}]}{\gamma_0}\right\}.
\]
The absolute standardized conditional mean is at most \(\bar c q_r^v\), because \(\varepsilon_Ca_r^{(Q)}\le1\).  Therefore
\[
 q_t^v\le\alpha^Q
 \prod_{r=t-\ell_t}^{t-1}(1-\bar c q_r^v)^{-1}. \tag{14}
\]
First using only \(q_r^v\le1\) in (14) gives
\[
 q_t^v\le\left(\frac{\alpha}{1-\bar c}\right)^Q=:r_0^Q,
 \qquad 0<r_0<1. \tag{15}
\]
Substitution of (15) back into (14), together with \(-\log(1-z)\le z/(1-z)\) for \(0\le z<1\), gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 q_t^v
 &\le\alpha^Q(1-\bar c r_0^Q)^{-Q}\\
 &\le\alpha^Q\exp\!\left\{
 \frac{\bar c}{1-\bar c}Qr_0^Q\right\}
 \le K_0\alpha^Q,
 \end{aligned} \tag{16}
\]
where
\[
 K_0:=\exp\!\left\{\frac{\bar c r_0}{(1-\bar c)(1-r_0)^2}\right\}<\infty.
\]
The last inequality uses \(Qr_0^Q\le\sum_{j\ge1}jr_0^j=r_0/(1-r_0)^2\).  Both \(r_0\) and \(K_0\) depend only on \(\alpha\), hence only on \(t_0\).

It remains to compute observed-path divergence.  Conditional actions have the same law under both alternatives and contribute zero to the likelihood ratio.  Conditional on a common observed history, \(Y_t/\gamma_0\) is Rademacher with means
\[
 \eta_t^v:=\frac{E_v[Y_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}^{\mathrm{obs}}]}{\gamma_0}
 =v\bar c\varepsilon_Ca_t^{(Q)}q_t^v.
\]
For Rademacher laws with means \(r,s\), direct substitution into their two point masses and \(\log u\le u-1\) gives
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(\operatorname{Rad}(r)\|\operatorname{Rad}(s))
 \le\chi^2(\operatorname{Rad}(r)\|\operatorname{Rad}(s))
 =\frac{(r-s)^2}{1-s^2}. \tag{17}
\]
Equations (16)--(17), \(|\eta_t^{-1}|\le\bar c\), and \(q_t^{+1}+q_t^{-1}\le2K_0\alpha^Q\) imply
\[
 \operatorname{KL}\{\mathcal L_{+1}(Y_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}^{\mathrm{obs}})\|
 \mathcal L_{-1}(Y_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}^{\mathrm{obs}})\}
 \le\frac{4\bar c^2K_0^2}{1-\bar c^2}
 \varepsilon_C^2\alpha^{2Q}(a_t^{(Q)})^2. \tag{18}
\]
Under the plus law the actions remain independent Bernoulli\((p)\), so
\[
 E_{+1}[(a_t^{(Q)})^2]
 =p^{2(Q-\ell_t)}p^{\ell_t}=p^{2Q-\ell_t}\le p^Q=L^{-Q}. \tag{19}
\]
For finite positive-probability paths, the log likelihood ratio is the sum of the conditional log likelihood ratios.  Taking its plus-law expectation, then applying (18)--(19), proves
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(\mathbb P_{Q,+1}^{\mathrm{obs},T}\|\mathbb P_{Q,-1}^{\mathrm{obs},T})
 \le B_0T\varepsilon_C^2\alpha^{2Q}L^{-Q},
 \qquad
 B_0:=\frac{4\bar c^2K_0^2}{1-\bar c^2}.
\]
The displayed \(B_0\) depends only on \(t_0\) and is independent of \(C,Q,T,M_1,M_2\); scaling by \(\gamma_0\) has canceled from the likelihood calculation.
added_lemmas.justification: This closes the early kill test and keeps the squared overlap perturbation explicit in the observed-data testing modulus.
added_lemmas.gap: The proof controls stationary initial windows and hidden reset episodes without revealing latent times.
added_lemmas.consumer: It supplies the cardinality-uniform two-point divergence for the minimax converse.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(P_+\) and \(P_-\) be mutually absolutely continuous laws on one observed-data space, and suppose their target values are \(+a\) and \(-a\), where \(a>0\).  Write \(P_{+1}:=P_+\) and \(P_{-1}:=P_-\).  Then every measurable estimator \(\widehat\vartheta\) satisfies
\[
 \max_{v\in\{-1,+1\}}E_{P_v}[(\widehat\vartheta-va)^2]
 \ge\frac{a^2}{4}\exp\{-\operatorname{KL}(P_+\|P_-)\}.
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Put \(A=\int\sqrt{dP_+dP_-}\) and \(O=\int\min(dP_+,dP_-)\).  Mutual absolute continuity makes the likelihood ratio finite almost surely.  Jensen's inequality under \(P_+\) gives
\[
 A=E_{P_+}\!\left[\exp\!\left\{-\frac12\log\frac{dP_+}{dP_-}\right\}\right]
 \ge\exp\{-\operatorname{KL}(P_+\|P_-)/2\}.
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz gives \(A^2\le O(2-O)\le2O\), so
\[
 O\ge\frac12\exp\{-\operatorname{KL}(P_+\|P_-)\}.
\]
Classify an arbitrary estimator as plus when \(\widehat\vartheta\ge0\).  On every classification error the squared distance from the corresponding target \(\pm a\) is at least \(a^2\).  Pointwise in the two densities, every binary rule pays the smaller density, so the sum of its two error probabilities is at least \(O\).  Hence
\[
 \max_{v\in\{-1,+1\}}E_{P_v}[(\widehat\vartheta-va)^2]
 \ge\frac{a^2O}{2}
 \ge\frac{a^2}{4}\exp\{-\operatorname{KL}(P_+\|P_-)\},
\]
as claimed.
added_lemmas.justification: This isolates the exact two-point squared-error reduction used by both components of the minimax converse.
added_lemmas.gap: The reduction is elementary but must be a declared node because both lower-bound arguments invoke it.
added_lemmas.consumer: It converts the parametric and signed-depth divergence bounds into minimax risk lower bounds.

added_lemmas.statement:
There is a constant \(c_{\mathrm{par}}>0\), depending only on \(M_1\) and \(M_2\), such that for every \(T\ge1\) and every \(C\ge1\),
\[
 R_T(t_0,\zeta,C)\ge c_{\mathrm{par}}T^{-1}.
\]
The lower bound holds on a one-state binary-action subexperiment with \(b=e\) and independent scaled Rademacher rewards.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Take singleton observed and hidden state spaces, \(\mathcal A=\{0,1\}\), and \(b=e=(1/2,1/2)\).  The state never moves.  Its contraction coefficient is zero, its two stationary laws coincide, and both overlap assumptions hold for every \(t_0>0\), \(\zeta>0\), and \(C\ge1\).  Put \(\eta_T:=1/(4\sqrt T)\).  Under alternative \(v\in\{-1,+1\}\), let the rewards be independent with values \(\pm\gamma_0\) and standardized mean \(v\eta_T\).  Their conditional mean has magnitude \(\gamma_0\eta_T\le M_1\), and their conditional second moment is \(\gamma_0^2\le M_2\), so both alternatives belong to the model class and have the same supplied design.  Their target values are \(\theta_v=v\gamma_0\eta_T\).

For the present scaled Rademacher experiment, direct substitution into the two point masses and \(\log u\le u-1\) give
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(P_+\|P_-)
 \le T\frac{4\eta_T^2}{1-\eta_T^2}\le\frac4{15}.
\]
Apply \(\mathrm{lem{:}two\text{-}point\text{-}testing\text{-}overlap}\) with \(a=\gamma_0/(4\sqrt T)\).  Since the pair shares one design tag, every admissible tagged decision family restricts to an estimator in this two-point experiment.  Taking the supremum and then the infimum in \(\mathrm{def{:}minimax\text{-}risk}\) yields
\[
 R_T(t_0,\zeta,C)
 \ge\frac{\gamma_0^2e^{-4/15}}{64}\,T^{-1}.
\]
This proves the result with \(c_{\mathrm{par}}=\gamma_0^2e^{-4/15}/64>0\).
added_lemmas.justification: The parametric subexperiment supplies the unavoidable risk floor at equality and below the overlap elbow.
added_lemmas.gap: A local hidden-state lower bound alone vanishes at equality and cannot establish the full uniform frontier.
added_lemmas.consumer: It joins the equality endpoint to the hidden-state lower bound.

added_lemmas.statement:
Fix \(t_0>0\), \(\zeta>0\), and \(0<M_1<\sqrt{M_2}\), and put \(\beta:=2/(2+t_0\zeta)\).  There are constants \(0<c_{\mathrm{unif}}\le C_{\mathrm{unif}}<\infty\) and \(T_0<\infty\), depending only on \(t_0,\zeta,M_1,M_2\), such that, simultaneously for every \(C\ge1\) and \(T\ge T_0\),
\[
 c_{\mathrm{unif}}\left\{T^{-1}+T^{-\beta}q_C^{2(1-\beta)}\right\}
 \le R_T(t_0,\zeta,C)
 \le C_{\mathrm{unif}}\left\{T^{-1}+T^{-\beta}q_C^{2(1-\beta)}\right\}.
\]
The upper bound is attained by the observable tagged estimator \(\widehat\theta_{\kappa_T(C)}\). added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Put \(r:=\log(1/\alpha)=1/t_0\), \(D_0:=2r+\log L\), and \(x:=Tq_C^2\).  Since \(L=e^\zeta\),
\[
 \beta=\frac{2r}{D_0}=\frac2{2+t_0\zeta},
 \qquad
 1-\beta=\frac{\log L}{D_0}. \tag{22}
\]

For the upper bound, apply \(\mathrm{lem{:}moment\text{-}phiw\text{-}radius\text{-}bound}\).  Because \(L>1\), its geometric sum is bounded by \(L^{k+1}/(L-1)\).  If \(k\le T/2\), there is a constant \(A<\infty\), depending only on \(t_0,\zeta,M_1,M_2\), such that
\[
 \sup_{M\in\mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C)}
 E_M[(\widehat\theta_k-\theta(K,e))^2]
 \le A\{q_C^2\alpha^{2k}+T^{-1}L^k+T^{-1}\}. \tag{23}
\]
Choose \(T_0\) so large that \(\log T/D_0\le T/2\) for every \(T\ge T_0\).  Since \(0\le q_C<1\), the cap in \(\kappa_T(C)\) is then inactive whenever \(x>1\).

If \(x\le1\), \(\kappa_T(C)=0\), and (23) is at most a constant multiple of \(T^{-1}\), because \(q_C^2\le T^{-1}\).  If \(x>1\), set \(k=\lfloor\log x/D_0\rfloor\).  Then
\[
 \alpha^{2k}\le\alpha^{-2}x^{-\beta},
 \qquad
 L^k\le x^{1-\beta}. \tag{24}
\]
Consequently both nonparametric terms in (23) have the same value up to a fixed factor:
\[
 q_C^2x^{-\beta}=T^{-\beta}q_C^{2(1-\beta)},
 \qquad
 T^{-1}x^{1-\beta}=T^{-\beta}q_C^{2(1-\beta)}. \tag{25}
\]
Equations (23)--(25) prove the asserted uniform upper bound and exhibit the single observable estimator.  No alphabet cardinality enters any constant.

We turn to the converse.  The parametric component is \(\mathrm{lem{:}parametric\text{-}moment\text{-}floor}\).  For the hidden-state component, let \(B_0\) be the \(C\)-independent constant in \(\mathrm{lem{:}scaled\text{-}observed\text{-}path\text{-}kl}\).  Choose a finite \(x_0\ge1\), depending only on \(t_0,\zeta\), so that
\[
 Q_x:=\left\lceil D_0^{-1}\log(8B_0x)\right\rceil\ge1
\]
whenever \(x\ge x_0\).  The epsilon comparison in \(\mathrm{lem{:}scaled\text{-}signed\text{-}depth\text{-}radius}\) and the explicit KL modulus give
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(\mathbb P_{Q_x,+1}^{\mathrm{obs},T}\|\mathbb P_{Q_x,-1}^{\mathrm{obs},T})
 \le B_0T\varepsilon_C^2e^{-D_0Q_x}
 \le B_0xe^{-D_0Q_x}\le\frac18. \tag{26}
\]
The same membership lemma gives target values \(\pm a_Q\), where \(a_Q=c_0\varepsilon_Cw_Q\), and
\[
 w_Q=\frac{(1-\alpha)\alpha^Q}{1-\alpha^{Q+1}}
 \ge(1-\alpha)\alpha^Q. \tag{27}
\]
The testing inequality \(\mathrm{lem{:}two\text{-}point\text{-}testing\text{-}overlap}\) applies directly to this common-design pair.  The ceiling defining \(Q_x\) gives
\[
 \alpha^{2Q_x}\ge\alpha^2(8B_0x)^{-\beta}. \tag{28}
\]
Using (26)--(28) and \(\varepsilon_C\ge q_C/2\), we obtain a constant \(c_{\mathrm{hid}}>0\), depending only on \(t_0,\zeta,M_1,M_2\), such that for \(x\ge x_0\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 R_T(t_0,\zeta,C)
 &\ge \frac14e^{-1/8}c_0^2\varepsilon_C^2(1-\alpha)^2\alpha^{2Q_x}\\
 &\ge c_{\mathrm{hid}}q_C^2x^{-\beta}
 =c_{\mathrm{hid}}T^{-\beta}q_C^{2(1-\beta)}.
 \end{aligned} \tag{29}
\]
The scaled signed-depth alternatives are bounded and binary-action members of the broader arbitrary-finite-action conditional-moment class.  Therefore their two-point lower bound transfers to the supremum over that class; no restriction of the upper theorem has been introduced.

If \(x<x_0\), the hidden term satisfies
\[
 T^{-\beta}q_C^{2(1-\beta)}=T^{-1}x^{1-\beta}
 \le x_0^{1-\beta}T^{-1},
\]
and is absorbed by the parametric lower bound.  If \(x\ge x_0\), the maximum of the parametric and hidden lower bounds is at least half their sum.  This proves the uniform lower inequality.  At \(C=1\), \(q_C=0\), so the law reduces to \(R_T\asymp T^{-1}\).  For each fixed \(C>1\), \(q_C\) is a positive constant and \(\beta<1\), so it reduces to \(R_T\asymp T^{-\beta}\).  These are respectively the equality and fixed-overlap corollaries of the same uniform theorem.  Finally, the ratio of the hidden term to \(T^{-1}\) is \(x^{1-\beta}\), so the unique elbow is \(Tq_C^2\asymp1\), equivalently \(q_C\asymp T^{-1/2}\).  The geometric covariance sum and the integer floor bounds introduce only constants, proving the absence of a logarithmic factor.

prose_updates.tldr: For Hu and Wager's single-trajectory conditional-moment POMDP class, strengthened by latent stationary overlap \(d_e\le Cd_b\), the exact cardinality-uniform minimax risk is \(R_T(t_0,\zeta,C)\asymp T^{-1}+T^{-\beta}q_C^{2(1-\beta)}\), uniformly for every \(C\ge1\), where \(q_C=(C-1)/C\) and \(\beta=2/(2+t_0\zeta)\). The comparison constants depend on \(t_0,\zeta,M_1,M_2\) but not on \(C\), \(T\), or alphabet cardinalities. Radius-adaptive observable PHIW attains the law, and a moment-scaled signed-depth pair gives the matching all-estimator converse. The exact elbow is \(q_C\asymp T^{-1/2}\), equivalently \(C_T-1\asymp T^{-1/2}\) near equality: equality is parametric, while every fixed \(C>1\) retains the Hu--Wager hidden-state exponent, with no logarithmic loss.

prose_updates.related_work: HuWager2023 is the theorem anchor: its Model 3 and Theorem 2.1 work with arbitrary finite actions and pointwise conditional first- and second-moment reward envelopes, while Theorem 3.1 gives the unrestricted single-trajectory exponent and Section 3.2 leaves a distributionally overlapping hidden-state converse open. The present upper theorem is proved on that conditional-moment class after adding only \(d_e\le Cd_b\); its hard scaled-Rademacher, binary-action family is a bounded subclass, so the converse transfers upward to the full moment class. The new result is the uniform radius law joining \(C=1\), shrinking \(C_T-1\), and fixed \(C>1\). MehrabiWager2025 remains a fully observed comparator because its stationary ratio is observable or estimable. ZhangJiang2024 and TennenholtzShalitMannor2020 require belief, proxy, rank, or decoupling structure absent here. KallusUehara2020 and LiaoKlasnjaMurphy2021 provide fully observed efficiency and mobile-health endpoints. The finite insulin construction adapts the LuckettEtAl2020 and MaahsEtAl2012 setting used in HuWager2023 Section 5.2; it does not assert that the original continuous simulator satisfies this finite-state contraction and overlap class.
prose_updates.interpretation: A latent occupancy assurance has a quantitative value only through its distance from equality. Near \(d_e=d_b\), it permits shorter observable histories and reaches parametric precision once \(q_C=O(T^{-1/2})\). A fixed nonunit bound, even if substantively small, leaves the worst-case hidden-state exponent unchanged when latent cardinality is unrestricted. The refreshed discretization has rewards in \([-1,0]\), so it fits the re-anchored moment envelope, for example with \(M_1=1\) and any \(M_2>1\). In that insulin illustration, bounded latent physiological occupancy therefore does not by itself justify immediate weighting; shorter histories require an assurance that tightens with trajectory length or additional observed state or proxy information.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The observed-filtration posterior recursion, stationary initial-window calculation, explicit \(T\varepsilon_C^2\alpha^{2Q}L^{-Q}\) KL modulus, conditional-moment PHIW covariance bound, uniform frontier, and interval-certified finite insulin demonstration are now proved in the note's core. The finite insulin model remains an artificial refreshed discretization, and no claim is made that the original continuous simulator in HuWager2023 or LuckettEtAl2020 satisfies finite-state uniform contraction or latent stationary overlap. The theorem is a mean-squared-error result and does not supply confidence intervals or a test of the latent-overlap assertion.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The theorem covers one stationary trajectory, arbitrary finite observed, hidden, and action alphabets with no cardinality bounds, Hu and Wager's conditional first- and second-moment reward envelope, known memoryless policies, uniform contraction, and latent joint-state stationary overlap. Its constants are uniform over \(C\ge1\) and may depend only on \(t_0,\zeta,M_1,M_2\). The hard family is binary and bounded but is used only as a subclass for the converse; the upper bound holds on the full moment class. The result does not cover a uniformly bounded hidden alphabet, nonstationary starts, unknown policies, proxy-assisted estimators, confidence intervals, policy-learning regret, or the original continuous insulin simulator. The refreshed \(360\)-state illustration demonstrates the interpretation but is not itself a minimax-hard sequence.
